result.title: Discrete Action Matching: Learning Stochastic Dynamics from Samples via State Graphs
result.summary: Learning population dynamics from unpaired temporal marginals is an ill-posed inverse problem that requires structural assumptions on the underlying dynamics. We introduce $\textit{Discrete Action Matching}$ (DAM), a finite-state counterpart of Action Matching based on discrete Wasserstein geometry. For a prescribed marginal path and transport geometry, we derive an action-minimization objective for its canonical minimum-kinetic-energy current. Our key observation is that the density dependence of the discrete action reduces to neighboring density ratios. Along an empirical interpolation of the snapshots, DAM first estimates these ratios and then learns an action potential. The learned fields also define a graph-supported Markov sampler. Experiments on controlled synthetic dynamics and real mouse gastrulation data evaluate marginal reconstruction and interpolation. Additional experiments approximate numerical surface-transport paths from paired samples.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Discrete Action Matching（DAM），在有限状态空间上以离散 Wasserstein 几何和状态图建模，从无配对的时间边缘分布中学习随机动力学，并给出基于图支撑的 Markov 采样器与插值实验。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「状态图上的密度比—动作势」表述可能与 LVR 的 latent 状态转移、轨迹训练与证据/信念状态更新存在概念联系，是否可用于建模 latent 推理状态演化尚需核查。
